page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 7559 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for multi-core processing, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 145373.21 and a PassMark CPU score of 128741.43. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching top-tier status in both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and database operations also perform in the top tier, as evidenced by PassMark encryption tests and a Redis SET throughput of 196.23 million operations per second. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D128lds_v7 maximizes compute density and high-speed local storage capacity at the expense of memory depth. The 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a clear tradeoff, making this instance less suitable for memory-bound in-memory databases, but highly cost-effective for compute-heavy workloads that require rapid local disk access. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, large-scale text processing, static web serving, ray tracing, and multi-threaded data decompression.
